n: John, an eyewitness Apostle, opens like his Gospel: he writes about Jesus, the Word of life who existed from the beginning. He stresses that the Apostles heard, saw, and even touched Him—Jesus was truly flesh.

f.g: Christ, the living message of God.

n: In a side note, John explains that eternal life—Christ Himself, who was with the Father—became visible, and the Apostles testify of Him.
John shares his witness so readers can join the Apostles in fellowship—a fellowship that is really with the Father and the Son.
He writes so that their joy—and his—may be complete.
The core message: God is light, with no darkness at all. Light stands for truth, goodness, and holiness.
If we claim closeness to God while living in sin, we are lying and not living by the truth.
But if we live in God’s light, we have true fellowship with each other, and Jesus’s blood keeps cleansing us from every sin.

f.w: blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us

n: Claiming we have no sin is self-deception. Honesty about our weaknesses is where repentance begins.
A promise to treasure: if we confess our sins, God is faithful and fair to forgive us and wash away all wrongdoing.
Denying that we have ever sinned effectively calls God a liar, since His word says all need a Savior.
